about: The datapoints to check by hand before the sets are trusted and grown: a stratified sample chosen by seed, 20 of the SQL set spread over its kinds and 10 of the chart set spread over its shapes. Rewrite it with `uv run finquery-bench sample --seed N`.

datapoints.question: Compare what I sent Anna with what I sent Max.
datapoints.why: Both payments are PayPal, so the counterparty is PayPal and the name is in the booking text. Matching the counterparty alone finds neither of them, and a CASE over that text that labels them is refused by the guard, so the two rows are a UNION of two branches.
datapoints.sql: SELECT 'Anna' AS person, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%anna weber%') UNION ALL SELECT 'Max' AS person, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%max schulz%')

datapoints.question: Was habe ich 2025 fuer Mobilfunk ausgegeben, also reine Handykosten ohne Festnetz?
datapoints.why: Modelle verwechseln oft Kategorie (Communication) und Subkategorie (Mobile).
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' AND subcategory = 'Mobile'

datapoints.question: Compare my spending on Public transport versus Ride hailing in 2025.
datapoints.why: Comparing two distinct subcategories within a single category
datapoints.sql: SELECT subcategory, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' AND category = 'Transport' AND subcategory IN ('Public transport', 'Ride hailing') GROUP BY subcategory

datapoints.question: What did I spend each month at Vapiano in Berlin Mitte during 2025, and how many visits was that?
datapoints.why: Calculates both monthly spending and monthly visit frequency for VAPIANO Berlin Mitte
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur, COUNT(*) AS visits FROM transaction_view WHERE amount < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' AND lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%vapiano%' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

datapoints.question: What was the single biggest one?
prefix: What were my total expenses in November 2025?
datapoints.why: Inherits November 2025 and finds the single largest spending booking (ORDER BY amount ASC LIMIT 1).
datapoints.sql: SELECT coalesce(counterparty, description) AS merchant, ROUND(-amount, 2) AS biggest_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-11-01' AND '2025-11-30' ORDER BY amount ASC LIMIT 1

datapoints.question: Wie viel habe ich im Dezember 2025 fuer die Subkategorie Supermarket bezahlt?
datapoints.why: Uses subcategory column instead of category for Supermarket in the specified month.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-12-01' AND '2025-12-31' AND subcategory = 'Supermarket'

datapoints.question: und wieviel davon war im supermarkt?
prefix: Wie viel habe ich im November 2025 fuer Lebensmittel ausgegeben?
datapoints.why: period: November 2025, inherited from the question before it; filters: of the Groceries bookings only the Supermarket ones, which is a subcategory and belongs in subcategory; sign: spending, amount < 0 reported positive; grouping: none, one figure.
datapoints.sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE
  amount < 0
  AND subcategory = 'Supermarket'
  AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-11-01' AND '2025-11-30'
LIMIT 200

datapoints.question: What have I spent per month since the summer?
datapoints.why: period: since the summer means from the start of June in the year the data covers to the newest booking, 2025-06-01 to 2025-12-28; filters: none beyond the sign; sign: spending, amount < 0 reported positive; grouping: one row per month, in order.
datapoints.sql:
SELECT
  STRFTIME('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month,
  ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE
  amount < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-06-01' AND '2025-12-28'
GROUP BY
  month
ORDER BY
  month
LIMIT 200

datapoints.question: What did Netflix take from me this quarter?
datapoints.why: period: this quarter is the range the household paragraph spells out, 2025-10-01 to 2025-12-31; filters: the merchant Netflix as one LIKE term over the booking text and the counterparty together; sign: spending, amount < 0 reported positive; grouping: none, one figure.
datapoints.sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE
  amount < 0
  AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-10-01' AND '2025-12-31'
  AND LOWER(description || ' ' || COALESCE(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%netflix%'
LIMIT 200

datapoints.question: Break my December 2025 spending down by category, and show me what has no category yet.
datapoints.why: period: December 2025, the month the question names; filters: none, every spending booking of that month counts; sign: spending, amount < 0 reported positive; grouping: one row per category, and the bookings without one are the Needs review bucket the question asks for by name.
datapoints.sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(category, 'Needs review') AS topic,
  ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE
  amount < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-12-01' AND '2025-12-31'
GROUP BY
  topic
ORDER BY
  total_eur DESC
LIMIT 200

datapoints.question: Wie haben sich meine Supermarktausgaben pro Monat entwickelt?
datapoints.why: period: none is named, so every month the data covers; filters: the subcategory Supermarket, which is the part of Groceries the question means and not the bakery or the drugstore; sign: spending, amount < 0 reported positive; grouping: one row per month, in order.
datapoints.sql:
SELECT
  STRFTIME('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month,
  ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE
  amount < 0 AND subcategory = 'Supermarket'
GROUP BY
  month
ORDER BY
  month
LIMIT 200

datapoints.question: Welche Zahlungen gehen jeden Monat raus, und wie viel sind das pro Anbieter im Jahr?
datapoints.why: period: das Jahr 2025, also der ganze Datenbereich; filters: nur Empfaenger, die in allen zwoelf Monaten vorkommen, denn genau das heisst jeden Monat; sign: Ausgabe, amount < 0 und positiv berichtet; grouping: eine Zeile pro Empfaenger, nie eine pro Buchung.
datapoints.sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(counterparty, description) AS merchant,
  ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur,
  COUNT(*) AS bookings
FROM transaction_view
WHERE
  amount < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31'
GROUP BY
  merchant
HAVING
  COUNT(DISTINCT STRFTIME('%Y-%m', booked_on)) = 12
ORDER BY
  total_eur DESC
LIMIT 200

datapoints.question: Did the money reaching me from January to June 2025 add up to more than from July to December?
datapoints.why: period: two halves of 2025, January to June against July to December; filters: none; sign: income, amount > 0; grouping: one row per half, because a comparison of two periods is two rows and never one number.
datapoints.sql:
SELECT
  CASE WHEN booked_on <= '2025-06-30' THEN 'first half' ELSE 'second half' END AS period,
  ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS income_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE
  amount > 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31'
GROUP BY
  period
ORDER BY
  period
LIMIT 200

datapoints.question: What did I spend last quarter, all in?
datapoints.why: period: last quarter is counted from the newest booking and not from today, so it is the range the household paragraph spells out, 2025-07-01 to 2025-09-30; filters: none, the whole household; sign: spending, amount < 0 reported positive; grouping: none, one figure.
datapoints.sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE
  amount < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-07-01' AND '2025-09-30'
LIMIT 200

datapoints.question: Zeig mir die Ausgaben im Dezember 2025 nach Kategorie und dazu die Gesamtsumme.
datapoints.why: period: Dezember 2025; filters: keine, jede Ausgabenbuchung des Monats zaehlt; sign: Ausgaben, amount < 0 positiv berichtet; grouping: eine Zeile pro Kategorie mit den unkategorisierten Buchungen als eigenem Eimer, dazu eine Zeile Gesamt, weil die Frage beides will.
datapoints.sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(category, 'Needs review') AS topic,
  ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE
  amount < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-12-01' AND '2025-12-31'
GROUP BY
  topic
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'Gesamt' AS topic,
  ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE
  amount < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-12-01' AND '2025-12-31'
LIMIT 200

datapoints.question: Which categories cost me the most last quarter? The top three.
datapoints.why: period: last quarter is the range the household paragraph spells out, 2025-07-01 to 2025-09-30, not the quarter today falls in; filters: none; sign: spending, amount < 0 reported positive; grouping: one row per category, sorted by the total and cut at three.
datapoints.sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(category, 'Needs review') AS topic,
  ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE
  amount < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-07-01' AND '2025-09-30'
GROUP BY
  topic
ORDER BY
  total_eur DESC
LIMIT 3

datapoints.question: Welche Zahlungsempfaenger stecken hinter den Buchungen, die noch keine Kategorie haben?
datapoints.why: period: none is named, so the whole range; filters: the bookings the household never categorized, which is category IS NULL, the Needs review bucket; sign: spending, amount < 0, reported positive; grouping: one row per counterparty, never one per booking.
datapoints.sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(counterparty, description) AS merchant,
  COUNT(*) AS bookings,
  ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE
  amount < 0 AND category IS NULL
GROUP BY
  merchant
ORDER BY
  total_eur DESC
LIMIT 200

datapoints.question: Which three shops swallowed the most of my grocery money in 2025?
datapoints.why: period: the year 2025; filters: the category Groceries, the household's own topic rather than a list of shop names; sign: spending, amount < 0 reported positive; grouping: one row per merchant, sorted by the total and cut at three.
datapoints.sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(counterparty, description) AS merchant,
  ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE
  amount < 0
  AND category = 'Groceries'
  AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31'
GROUP BY
  merchant
ORDER BY
  total_eur DESC
LIMIT 3

datapoints.question: Und welcher von den fuenf war der kleinste Posten?
prefix: Welche fuenf Empfaenger haben 2025 am meisten von mir bekommen?
datapoints.why: period: 2025, inherited from the question before it; filters: the same five recipients that question ranked, which are the ones over 900 euro; sign: spending, amount < 0, reported positive; grouping: one row per recipient, sorted upwards because the smallest of the five is asked for, cut at one.
datapoints.sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(counterparty, description) AS merchant,
  ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS smallest_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE
  amount < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31'
GROUP BY
  merchant
HAVING
  ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) >= 900
ORDER BY
  smallest_eur ASC
LIMIT 1

datapoints.question: What did my Kaufland shopping add up to over 2025?
datapoints.why: period: the year 2025, which the question names and which is the whole range of this data; filters: the merchant Kaufland, matched case-insensitively over the booking text and the counterparty together; sign: spending, so amount < 0 and the total is reported positive; grouping: none, the answer is one figure.
datapoints.sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE
  amount < 0
  AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31'
  AND LOWER(description || ' ' || COALESCE(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%kaufland%'
LIMIT 200

datapoints.question: Draw a sankey of how my 2025 spending flows from its categories into their subcategories.
datapoints.why: A flow whose two ends are both columns of the view. Rows without a subcategory have no target, and a link with one end missing refuses the whole graph.
datapoints.sql: SELECT category AS source, subcategory AS target, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS amount_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' AND category IS NOT NULL AND subcategory IS NOT NULL GROUP BY source, target ORDER BY amount_eur DESC

datapoints.question: Welche Streaming- und Abo-Dienste haben mich 2025 am meisten gekostet? Zeig mir die Rangliste im Diagramm.
datapoints.why: Explicit merchant matching for subscriptions ranked by annual spending.
datapoints.sql: SELECT coalesce(title, counterparty, description) AS merchant, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' AND (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%netflix%' OR lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%spotify%' OR lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%prime%' OR lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%adobe%') GROUP BY merchant ORDER BY total_eur DESC

datapoints.question: Show me for each month of 2025 how much more or less I spent than the month before.
datapoints.why: The signed figure this year really draws on both sides of the baseline: six months cheaper than the one before them and five dearer. A bar rests on zero by itself, so the zero line sits inside the plot and a month in the red stays negative in the tooltip.
datapoints.sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, -SUM(amount) AS spent FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY month), stepped AS (SELECT month, spent, LAG(spent) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS before FROM monthly) SELECT month, ROUND(spent - before, 2) AS change_eur FROM stepped WHERE before IS NOT NULL ORDER BY month

datapoints.question: was hab ich 2025 jeden monat so ausgegeben? kurve bitte
datapoints.why:
die Anfrage ist deutsch, also language de
sie fragt nach dem Verlauf ueber die Monate
eine Linie liest so einen Verlauf am direktesten
die Spalten sind month und total_eur
der Zeitraum ist das ganze Jahr 2025
datapoints.sql:
SELECT
  STRFTIME('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month,
  ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE
  amount < 0
GROUP BY
  month
ORDER BY
  month
LIMIT 200

datapoints.question: Zeig mir, wie sich meine Ausgaben seit dem Sommer aufsummiert haben.
datapoints.why:
die Anfrage ist deutsch, also ist die Sprache de
aufsummiert heisst ein laufender Gesamtstand ueber die Monate
ein laufender Gesamtstand ist eine Flaeche
die Spalten sind der Monat und die aufaddierte Euro-Zahl, die Zahl zuletzt
seit dem Sommer ist der 2025-06-01 bis heute, 2025-12-31, aus den Daten des Haushalts gelesen
datapoints.sql:
WITH per_month AS (
  SELECT
    STRFTIME('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month,
    -SUM(amount) AS eur
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE
    amount < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-06-01' AND '2025-12-31'
  GROUP BY
    month
)
SELECT
  month,
  ROUND(SUM(eur) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS cumulative_eur
FROM per_month
ORDER BY
  month
LIMIT 200

datapoints.question: Die Baeckerei steht als Baeckerei Steinecke auf dem Auszug. Was hat die mich pro Quartal gekostet?
datapoints.why:
die Anfrage ist deutsch, also ist die Sprache de
vier Quartale nebeneinander, eine Zahl je Quartal
vier Werte liest man am besten als Balken, nicht als Linie
Baeckerei Steinecke ist angereichert der Titel Steinecke
die Spalten sind quarter und total_eur, der Zeitraum ist das Jahr 2025 in Quartalen
datapoints.sql:
SELECT
  '2025-Q' || (
    (
      CAST(STRFTIME('%m', booked_on) AS INTEGER) + 2
    ) / 3
  ) AS quarter,
  ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE
  amount < 0 AND title = 'Steinecke'
GROUP BY
  quarter
ORDER BY
  quarter
LIMIT 200

datapoints.question: Compare December 2025 with November across the categories I spend the most in.
datapoints.why:
the request is written in English, so language en
two periods are compared and the breakdown is by category, so two dimensions that cross
grouped bars put December beside November for each category
the period is the series and the category is the position, so the rows come long
an axis of names holds about six, so the six largest by total over both months
datapoints.sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(category, 'Needs review') AS topic,
    CASE WHEN booked_on >= '2025-12-01' THEN 'This month' ELSE 'Last month' END AS period,
    -amount AS eur
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE
    amount < 0 AND booked_on >= '2025-11-01' AND booked_on < '2026-01-01'
), big AS (
  SELECT
    topic
  FROM months
  GROUP BY
    topic
  ORDER BY
    SUM(eur) DESC
  LIMIT 6
)
SELECT
  topic,
  period,
  ROUND(SUM(eur), 2) AS total_eur
FROM months
WHERE
  topic IN (
    SELECT
      topic
    FROM big
  )
GROUP BY
  topic,
  period
ORDER BY
  topic,
  period
LIMIT 200

datapoints.question: Those grocery bars were one block. We had October and then the year; now take groceries again and show which shops the money went to, as a doughnut.
datapoints.why:
the request is written in English, so language en
the topic is inherited from the grocery turns, and this one asks how that one whole splits up
a share of a whole with a handful of names is a doughnut
the columns are the shop name and the euro figure, the figure last
the period is 2025, carried over from the turn before
datapoints.sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(title, counterparty, description) AS merchant,
  ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE
  amount < 0 AND category = 'Groceries'
GROUP BY
  merchant
ORDER BY
  total_eur DESC
LIMIT 6

datapoints.question: Show me month by month which categories my salary went to.
datapoints.why:
the request is written in English, so the language is en
it asks where the money went inside each month, so the month total matters as well
a stacked bar shows the month's total and its parts at once
the group is the household's own category column, with the uncategorized as 'Needs review'
the columns are month, topic and total_eur, the euro column last
datapoints.sql:
SELECT
  STRFTIME('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month,
  COALESCE(category, 'Needs review') AS topic,
  ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE
  amount < 0
GROUP BY
  month,
  topic
ORDER BY
  month,
  topic
LIMIT 200

datapoints.question: Show how the spending that is still in Needs review piles up over 2025, as an area.
datapoints.why:
the request is written in English, so language en
Needs review is the bucket of bookings with no category, never a category of its own
"piles up" is a running total, so an area over the months
the columns are the month and the running total, the euro figure last
the period is the whole year 2025
datapoints.sql:
SELECT
  month,
  ROUND(SUM(spent) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS cumulative_eur
FROM (
  SELECT
    STRFTIME('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month,
    -SUM(amount) AS spent
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE
    amount < 0
    AND category IS NULL
    AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31'
  GROUP BY
    month
)
ORDER BY
  month
LIMIT 200
